backend.unresponsive: The local engine is busy and not answering right now — it recovers on its own.
backend.unresponsive_remote: Can't confirm the connection to the remote engine — retrying automatically.
backend.unhealthy: The engine is answering but reports that it isn't healthy. Check Settings → Logs → Backend, then retry.
backend.auth_required: The remote engine no longer accepts this app's sign-in. Reconnect with its API key.
backend.port_in_use: Port {{port}} is already in use by another program. Close it, or set OMNIVOICE_PORT to a free port, then retry.
backend.failed: The local engine could not start.
backend.first_run_hint: First run can take several minutes while the Python environment is prepared.
backend.setup_hint: Download Python and app dependencies (several GB). Voice models are installed separately when you choose them.
backend.setup_space: Free at least {{gib}} GiB on the app’s drive, then retry.
backend.repair_failed: Automatic repair of the Python environment did not finish. Check the engine log, then press Retry.
backend.setup_access: Allow write access to the app’s data folder, then retry.
backend.setup_unsupported_platform: Connect this app to a remote backend below. PyTorch is not released for Intel macOS, so this Mac needs no local backend installation.
backend.setup_wrong_architecture: Quit VoiceStudio, replace it with the Apple Silicon (arm64) DMG, then open it again. You are running the Intel build through Rosetta; switching builds enables local AI without removing voices or projects.
backend.setup_missing_system_library: This Windows system is missing the Microsoft Visual C++ 2015-2022 Redistributable (x64), which the PyTorch audio extension needs. Install it from Microsoft, then press Retry.
backend.setup_outdated_system_library: This Windows system's Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable (x64) is too old, so a speech library crashes when it loads. Install the latest version from Microsoft, then press Retry.
backend.setup_files_locked: Another program is using VoiceStudio's files (OneDrive or another sync app, antivirus, or a VoiceStudio backend that is still running). Close it or pause syncing, then press Retry.
backend.proxy_bypass_help: Fully quit VoiceStudio, set HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY to your proxy URL and NO_PROXY to excluded hosts in a terminal, then launch VoiceStudio from that terminal. Retrying in the current app cannot load new environment variables.
backend.hint_spawn_blocked: Your operating system or security software refused to launch the local engine. Add VoiceStudio’s runtime folder to your antivirus exclusions (Windows: Windows Security → Virus & threat protection → Manage settings → Exclusions), make sure it is not inside a cloud-synced folder such as OneDrive, then retry.
backend.hint_smart_app_control: Windows Smart App Control blocked the local engine. It has no per-app exceptions, so an antivirus exclusion will not help. Turn it off in Windows Security → App & browser control → Smart App Control settings (Windows cannot turn it back on without a reset), or connect VoiceStudio to an engine running on another computer, then retry.
backend.hint_slow_start: The engine was still starting when the wait ran out. Slow computers — especially ones without a dedicated GPU — and the first launch after an install (antivirus scans every new file) can need several minutes. Close memory-heavy apps and retry; later starts are much faster.
backend.hint_synced_folder: This location is inside a cloud-synced folder (OneDrive, Dropbox, iCloud Drive, Google Drive). Online-only placeholders and file locking break the Python environment. Move VoiceStudio to a plain local folder (for example C:\VoiceStudio on Windows or ~/VoiceStudio on macOS and Linux) and set it up again.
backend.cause_smart_app_control: Windows Smart App Control blocked the engine
backend.cause_spawn_blocked: Security software blocked the engine from starting
backend.cause_native_crash: The engine crashed while starting (native fault)
backend.cause_missing_env: The Python environment is missing or incomplete
backend.cause_permission: No permission to write to the engine folder
backend.cause_synced_folder: The engine folder is inside a cloud-synced folder
backend.cause_slow_start: The engine is still starting on a slow computer

engines.asrSetupRemote: No installation is needed. Configure an OpenAI-compatible transcription server under Settings → Models → ASR; the server manages its own models.

engines.setupStatusLicense: License not accepted yet. Review and accept it in Settings → Models to enable this engine.
engines.setupStatusNeedsConfig: This engine needs to be configured before it can run. Open Settings → Models to finish setting it up.

engines.setupStatusPlatform: This engine doesn't run on this computer's platform. Its guide lists the platforms it supports.
engines.setupStatusNoMps: This engine needs Apple's GPU (MPS), and this installation's PyTorch can't use it. Updating macOS or reinstalling VoiceStudio usually restores it.
engines.asrSetupRepairBundled: The backend's bundled Python packages are missing or damaged. Repair the backend environment, or recreate it from the pinned source setup, then restart.

tts_errors.gpu_arch_unsupported: This PyTorch build does not support your GPU. Choose CPU in Settings → Performance & Device, or install a compatible PyTorch build.
tts_errors.windows_app_control_blocked: Windows application control blocked a required file. Ask your administrator to allow the trusted VoiceStudio runtime, then restart the app.
tts_errors.audio_io_failed: Audio could not be read or saved. Check the file format, free disk space, and file permissions. Review the folder in Settings → Storage.
tts_errors.no_audio_track: This file has no audio track, so there is no speech to transcribe, dub or clone. Choose a video or audio file that contains sound.
tts_errors.source_language_required: Speech recognition did not report which language this video is spoken in, so it can't be translated here. Open the video in Dubbing and choose its source language, or pick a speech recognition model that detects the language.
tts_errors.transcription_media_tool: Transcription needs ffmpeg, which VoiceStudio could not find or run. Open Settings → Audio tools and use Download/Repair, or install ffmpeg (macOS: brew install ffmpeg; Windows: winget install Gyan.FFmpeg; Linux: your package manager) and restart VoiceStudio. You can also point FFMPEG_PATH at an ffmpeg binary.
tts_errors.transcription_pipe_lost: The backend lost its output pipe to the app while transcribing (broken pipe). Restart VoiceStudio and try again.
tts_errors.gpu_oom: The GPU ran out of memory. Close other GPU-heavy apps or unload models, then retry. You can also choose CPU in Settings → Performance & Device or select a smaller TTS engine.
tts_errors.host_memory_exhausted: The computer ran out of memory. Close other memory-heavy apps and browser tabs, flush models you are not using, render a shorter passage, or select a lighter TTS engine.
tts_errors.disk_full: The disk is full. Free space on the drive that holds VoiceStudio's data, model cache or temp folder, then try again. Settings → Storage shows disk usage and can clear temporary files.
tts_errors.engine_dependency_missing: A Python package this engine needs is not installed, so the engine could not start. Open Settings → Models, select the engine and use Install / Repair, then restart VoiceStudio.
tts_errors.reference_stt_missing: This voice has no transcript and no speech-to-text model is installed to write one. Type what the reference clip says into the transcript box (clips up to 20 seconds), or install a speech-to-text model in Settings → Models, select it, then generate again.
tts_errors.proxy_gateway_error: A proxy or gateway between you and VoiceStudio answered HTTP {{status}} instead of the backend. The backend may still be working. Raise the proxy's read timeout (for nginx, proxy_read_timeout) for long generations, then check Settings → Logs → Backend.
tts_errors.route_not_found: The running VoiceStudio backend has no {{route}} endpoint. Restart VoiceStudio so the app and backend match; if it persists, update both to the same version.

dub.quality_title: Cinematic uses an LLM to translate, review, and adapt in three passes. Configure an LLM before using it.
dub.auto_glossary_title: One extra LLM pass reads the whole transcript and extracts the video's theme plus key terms, so names and terminology stay consistent across segments. Your manual glossary entries always win.
dub.reflect_title: After each segment's direct translation, the LLM critiques and rewrites it into natural spoken dialogue. Uses 3 LLM calls per segment instead of 1; if refinement fails, the direct translation is kept.
dub.condense_title: When a translated line is predicted not to fit its time slot, ask the LLM for a shorter meaning-preserving rewrite you can apply per segment. Off by default; needs a configured LLM.
dub.restore_title: Restore every segment to its original transcript
dub.clean_up_title: Join tiny fragments and neighboring short segments.

dub.timing_smart_fit_title: Splits the difference: slightly speeds up the audio (pitch preserved, up to 1.5×) and slightly slows down that segment of the video (up to 2×) so natural-rate speech fits. Anything beyond the caps is trimmed and flagged. Export re-encodes the video.
dub.fit_speed_hint: Smart Fit speed limits. Tighter limits keep speech natural; wider limits fit more lines without trimming. The defaults suit most videos.
dub.voice_match_title: Voice match — whether each dubbed line clones from its own source clip or every line of a speaker shares one reference.
dub.voice_match_per_line_title: Each line clones from a clip of its own source audio. Best per-line prosody match, but the voice identity can drift from line to line.
dub.voice_match_consistent_title: Every line of a speaker clones from one shared reference (the speaker clone, or the best single clip when none exists). Steadier voice identity across the whole dub.

settings.reset_tier_assets_hint: Model weights, sidecar engines, audio tools and caches. Everything you made stays. They re-download when next needed.
settings.reset_tier_everything_hint: Back to a fresh install: settings, voices, projects, audio, models, engines, logs. The app restarts on the first-run screen.

settings.llmp_desc: Powers Cinematic & Autofit translation — the LLM rewrites each line to fit its segment's time budget so the video timing holds. Keys are stored encrypted; local providers (Ollama/LM Studio) stay fully offline.
settings.llmp_catalogue_note: The provider marked active is what answers whenever the LLM engine family is set to OpenAI-compatible in the catalogue.
settings.llmp_catalogue_link: Open the LLM family in the catalogue
settings.llmp_provider_hint: Pick a provider to configure. The active one is used for Cinematic/Autofit translation. Local providers need no key but require their server to be running.
settings.llmp_key_env: set via environment (.env) — overrides this field
settings.llmp_saved_not_active: Saved — not yet used for translation. Click “Save & use for translation” to switch.
settings.llmp_setup_hint: Choose a provider, start its server or add its API key, then connect. VoiceStudio verifies a model response before enabling LLM features.
settings.llmp_err_config: Complete the provider settings: Base URL, model, and any required API key or account ID.
settings.llmp_err_auth: Key rejected (401/403) — check your API key.
settings.llmp_err_not_found: Not found (404) — check the model name and Base URL path.
settings.llmp_err_rate_limit: Rate-limited (429) — the key works; try again in a moment.
settings.llmp_err_network: Can't reach the provider — check the Base URL, your network, or that the local server is running.
settings.llmp_env_override: set via an environment variable — overrides this field
settings.llmp_active_env_pin: The language model is set by an environment variable on this computer, so it can't be changed here.
settings.llmp_models_truncated: first {{count}} shown — type to narrow the model name
settings.llmskills_desc: Route each AI-powered feature to its own LLM — keep sensitive work on a local model (Ollama/LM Studio) while heavier jobs use a remote provider — or switch a feature off entirely. Off behaves exactly like having no LLM configured: the feature falls back to its non-LLM path.
settings.llmskills_dub_translation_desc: Translates dub lines directly with your configured LLM provider (the Dubbing tab's 'LLM' engine). Off: the LLM engine is unavailable — pick another engine.
settings.llmskills_cinematic_translation_desc: Rewrites each translated line for natural, in-character delivery (and Autofit's time budget). Off: dubs use the Fast translation result.
settings.llmskills_slot_fitting_desc: Trims or expands a translated line so its reading time fits the segment's time slot. Off: the line is used as-is.
settings.llmskills_glossary_extract_desc: Proposes project glossary terms (names, places, recurring terminology) from the source segments. Off: add glossary terms manually.
settings.llmskills_direction_parse_desc: Turns a natural-language delivery note ("more urgent, surprised") into structured voice-direction tokens. Off: a fast keyword heuristic is used instead.
settings.llmskills_dictation_refinement_desc: Cleans final dictation transcripts — filler words, self-corrections, punctuation. Off: the raw transcript passes through unchanged.
settings.audio_tools_desc: The media engine (FFmpeg, FFprobe) and video downloader (yt-dlp) the app manages for you.
settings.audio_tools_manual_hint: Prefer your package manager? Install FFmpeg yourself (macOS: brew install ffmpeg · Debian/Ubuntu: sudo apt install ffmpeg · Windows: winget install ffmpeg) and press Use system copy. Nothing is ever installed system-wide by the app.
settings.audio_tools_ffmpeg_desc: Converts, dubs, and mixes audio/video. The app resolves it automatically — override only if you need a specific build.
settings.audio_tools_ffprobe_desc: Reads media metadata (durations, frame rates) for Smart Fit and imports.
settings.audio_tools_ytdlp_desc: Powers video/clip imports. Site support changes faster than app releases — update it here when imports start failing.
settings.audio_tools_ytdlp_updated: yt-dlp {{version}} installed — restart the backend to apply.
settings.audio_tools_ytdlp_restored: Tested yt-dlp restored — restart the backend to apply.
settings.audio_tools_moved_note: The FFmpeg override moved to its own panel with more control (version, origin, restore).
settings.translation_providers_desc: Keys for the online translators: Google Cloud, DeepL, Microsoft Azure and AWS. Saved on this computer and kept across restarts.

settings.remote_backend_recovery_hint: You can change the remote backend later in Settings → Sharing.

settings.remote_backend_error_cors: The remote backend blocked this app. Allow this app's origin in the backend CORS settings.
settings.remote_backend_error_network: The remote backend could not be reached. Check its address, network, and firewall.
settings.remote_backend_error_timeout: The remote backend did not respond in time.
settings.remote_backend_error_wrong_port: This does not look like the VoiceStudio HTTP API. Port 7443 is usually the remote-worker control port; try port 3900.

settings.perf_torch_compile_note: Uses eager execution, without compiled kernels, when Triton is unstable.

settings.compute_device_restart: Takes effect after the app restarts
settings.generate_timeout_gpu_note: Used when generation runs on CUDA, ROCm, MPS, or another accelerator. Also used for CPU-family generation if no CPU budget below is set.
settings.generate_budget_desc: How long one generation may run before it is abandoned as too heavy for this hardware. CPU renders are legitimately slower than accelerated ones, so they get their own, higher floor.
settings.compute_device_desc: Which device the backend runs models on. Auto is right for almost everyone.
settings.compute_device_ignored: That device was not detected on this machine — Auto is in effect
settings.history_retention_cap_hint: Starred takes never count against cleanup · 0 = unlimited
settings.history_retention_help: After each generation, the oldest unstarred takes over this limit are removed along with their audio files. Starred takes are always kept. Set 0 to keep everything.

crash.details_intro_unclean: The previous run's shutdown marker was never cleared, {{ago}} ago. VoiceStudio cannot tell whether it crashed or was simply interrupted — sleeping, force-quitting, or stopping a VM/container leaves the same trace. If everything works now, nothing needs doing.

errors.title: This tab hit a snag.
errors.desc: Don't worry — the rest of the app still works. You can switch tabs, or try again below.
errors.crash_port_in_use: The backend could not start because port 3900 is already in use — another copy of VoiceStudio (or an app that claimed that port) is holding it. Quit the other instance and relaunch; if nothing is visibly running, an orphaned backend from a previous session is still holding the port.
errors.crash_oom_kill: It was force-killed (signal 9), which usually means the operating system ran out of memory (RAM) and stopped it. Close memory-heavy apps, pick a smaller ASR model in Settings → Models, or flush the TTS model before transcribing.
errors.crash_native_fault: It crashed inside the compute stack rather than running out of memory — that points at a GPU driver that does not match the bundled CUDA runtime, or a model file that downloaded incompletely. Update your GPU driver, then re-download the model from Settings → Models (it repairs a partial download in place). If it keeps happening, switch to a crash-isolated engine in Settings → Models — "VoiceStudio (subprocess)" for synthesis, "Faster-Whisper (crash-isolated subprocess)" for transcription. Those run the model in a separate process, so a crash like this takes down that process instead of the whole backend.
errors.report_failed: Couldn't open the bug report. Please try again, or copy the details above into a new issue.
errors.backend_shutting_down: VoiceStudio is shutting down. Reopen the app and try again.
errors.crash_broken_env: It died while loading its own Python dependencies, so this is not about memory or your GPU — the environment is incomplete or was left half-updated. Use "Clean & Retry" in Settings → Logs → Backend, which rebuilds it from scratch; that repairs it in place, without touching your voices or projects. If it still fails afterwards, the crash details name the exact package that would not import.
errors.crash_vram_default: On smaller GPUs the usual cause is running out of VRAM while loading the ASR model on top of the TTS model: flush the TTS model first, or pick a smaller ASR model in Settings → Models.
errors.stream_cut_backend_alive: Start with whatever sits between the browser and the app, such as a reverse proxy or load balancer. For this route, disable response buffering (proxy_buffering off; X-Accel-Buffering: no) and lengthen the read timeout. The stream was severed while the backend kept running, so the app did not crash. This most often happens behind a proxy on a hosted or containerized setup; launching the desktop app directly, or using localhost, will tell you whether the proxy is responsible.

failureClass.appimage_webkit_whitescreen: The window stayed blank. Start VoiceStudio with WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER=1.
failureClass.broken_venv: VoiceStudio's Python environment is damaged. Restart the app to rebuild it.
failureClass.clone_reference_missing: This voice has no reference audio. Pick a voice with a saved clip, or add a few seconds of clear speech.
failureClass.compute_type_unsupported: Your GPU can't run this precision. Choose CPU or another device.
failureClass.diarization_load_failed: The speaker model failed to load. Check the backend log, then retry.
failureClass.diarization_model_missing: The speaker model isn't installed. Install or repair it, then retry.
failureClass.gatekeeper_quarantine: macOS blocked the app. Clear its quarantine flag (xattr -cr), then reopen it.
failureClass.hf_auth_failed: Hugging Face refused access. Add a valid token, and accept the model's terms if it's gated.
failureClass.hf_mirror_unreachable: The Hugging Face mirror can't be reached. Check the mirror setting or use the official endpoint.
failureClass.input_too_short: The text or reference clip is too short for this engine. Add a few words or use a longer clip.
failureClass.invalid_media_file: This media file is damaged or incomplete. Use a file that plays, or download it again.
failureClass.media_tool_missing: ffmpeg isn't available. Download or repair it in Audio tools, then retry.
failureClass.model_cache_corrupt: A model file is damaged. Retry to repair it; if it persists, reinstall the model.
failureClass.model_download_interrupted: A model download was cut off. Retry; it resumes where it stopped.
failureClass.os_invalid_argument: The system refused to write a temporary file. Check that the temp folder exists and has free space.
failureClass.pkg_resources_missing: A Python setup file is missing, often removed by antivirus. Reinstall setuptools, then restart.
failureClass.pockettts_gated_weights: PocketTTS needs Hugging Face access. Accept its terms on Hugging Face and add your token.
failureClass.pyannote_license_required: The speaker model needs its licence accepted on Hugging Face. Accept it and add your token.
failureClass.socks_proxy_support_missing: A SOCKS proxy is set but not supported. Update VoiceStudio or unset the proxy.
failureClass.ssl_handshake_failure: A proxy or antivirus is intercepting secure connections. Update VoiceStudio or allow it there.
failureClass.tls_connection_dropped: The secure connection dropped. Retry; if it repeats, try without a VPN.
failureClass.transformers_import: A speech component failed to load. Check the backend log for the cause.
failureClass.unsupported_video_url: This link isn't a video page. Paste a direct video link, or upload the file.
failureClass.video_download_bot_check: YouTube asks for a signed-in check. Attach a cookies.txt export in Dub, or upload the file.
failureClass.video_download_network: The video download dropped. Retry; if it repeats, check your network.
failureClass.video_download_os_error: The video couldn't be saved. Check free space and that the data folder is writable.
failureClass.video_drm_protected: This video is DRM-protected and can't be downloaded. Try again later or upload the file.
failureClass.windows_paging_file_too_small: Windows needs a larger paging file for this model. Set it to at least 32 GB and restart, or use a smaller engine.
failureClass.windows_untrusted_mount: Windows blocked a folder on an untrusted drive. Move the data folder to a regular local drive.
